_note: Draft Duel: best of 7 (the first to win wins_needed rounds wins; at most max_rounds, then most wins, or a draw). Each round, both players make picks_per_round picks: in round 1, starting animals from their collection; after that, from offer_count options (animals and tools from the collection, at most offer_tools_max tools and at least offer_tools_min when there are any; rarer cards come up less, by rarity_weights). A pick takes an offered animal (one you have gets a star instead), takes an offered tool (at most tools_max; a third replaces one), or adds a star to a herd animal. Stars go up to star_max; each star after the first adds star_bonus_pct to health and bite. No limit on the herd. Tools can be used once in every fight. Times are in seconds, distances in tiles; the fighting itself is tuned in battle_rules.json and classes.json.

bot._note: How the computer opponent weighs a pick (scripts/draft/draft_bot.gd): a new animal starts at new_animal, a star at star, a tool at tool (plus tool_per_animal for each animal in its herd, at most 2; tool_swap when its belt is full). A card's power (its cost in animals.json, from 2 to 8) adds power per point above an ordinary 4.5. A class its herd doesn't have yet adds new_class; counters against your herd add up to 4 more. A Rival's style and some luck do the rest.

field._note: The field grows for big herds, keeping its shape, and the camera zooms out to show all of it. scale 1 is 16 x 20 tiles. It starts growing when the bigger herd has more than grow_from_units animals on the field (a pack counts each animal) and reaches max_scale at grow_full_units; it also grows if the rows wouldn't fit otherwise. max_scale is the camera's zoom limit: animals are drawn 1/max_scale as big at most, so they stay readable on a phone. edge: how far (tiles) the last line stays from the back of the field.
